solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Against having a man to follow Penny in charge of current affairs

blocks.note: against as in 'shoulder to the wheel': up against, touching
P is the abbreviation for a penny
IC is short for 'in charge'; here the 'in' doubles as placement
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a man succeeding Penny as the editor responsible for the current affairs desk.
explanation.walkthrough: IC is the standard abbreviation for 'in charge'; the man (AL) follows the penny and the charge, after TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical deals with matters of present interest, the news of the day.

clue.text: Delicacy shown in piece supporting flyer

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means holding up from below, so the piece is written underneath the flyer

blocks.note: a tit is a small bird
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A dainty morsel served on a stand beneath a bird ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supporting' puts the piece underneath the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty morsel of food, a delicacy.

clue.text: Drink extremely lively stout

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outer letters

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
the first and last letters of lively

explanation.surface: A drink that is very lively stout, as in a dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the beer; it is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly and stout both describe a rather fat, round figure.

clue.text: Gossip columnist's debut with article on fellow consumed by passion

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter
consumed by means swallowed up inside something else

blocks.note: the first letter of columnist
the heat of passion
W is the abbreviation for with
the definite article
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A gossip columnist's first piece about a man overcome by love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here: it supplies its abbreviation, and everything after the first letter goes inside the passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew the fat is an informal idiom for chatting at leisure.

clue.text: Released particulars about penning book on the Queen

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards
penning means enclosing as in a pen, so other letters go inside

blocks.note: details are particulars
B is the abbreviation for book
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Detailed reports about writing a book on the monarch have been made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated and released both mean set free.

clue.text: Ship's mate's uncertain about turning back

indicators.note: uncertain letters are unsettled, so they can be rearranged
turning back means the short word is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters of mate's, treated as fodder
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sailor on a ship is unsure about turning round and heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Ship's is a link ('is'), while the 's of mate's is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a vessel driven by steam power, a type of ship.

clue.text: Consider including priest in a night on the razzle?

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so a part goes inside

blocks.note: to see is to consider
PR is an abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: Should a priest be invited to join a wild night out?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a spree need not be at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of wild partying, and being on the razzle is British slang for a night of revelry.

clue.text: Fair result for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an event is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A just outcome, on the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means fair and balanced, as in an even contest.

clue.text: Extremely foolish to reject Irish girl's song

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the abbreviation is turned round

blocks.note: mad means very foolish
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
gal is informal for girl

explanation.surface: It would be mad to turn down an Irish girl's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an end-letters signal, but 'Extremely foolish' simply means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for several unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Dearer if represented as exclusive

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something costlier comes across as more select.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied describes something select and remote from ordinary people, like an exclusive circle.

clue.text: Curt is somewhat bitter secretly

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: found inside bitTER SEcretly

explanation.surface: A short-tempered person is quietly rather bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt and terse both describe speech that is brief to the point of rudeness.

clue.text: One serving of cake at present

blocks.note: a cake of soap or chocolate is a bar
to tender is to present or offer, as in tendering a payment

explanation.surface: Someone handing out a slice of cake at a gift-giving occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One serving of cake' reads as a portion; 'One serving' is the definition, a person who serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender is the person who serves drinks behind a bar.

clue.text: Unlucky tsar shot by hostile revolutionary

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ill as in ill will: unfriendly
the letters to be rearranged
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: An ill-fated tsar gunned down by a hostile revolutionary, as Nicholas II was.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred means born under an unlucky star, hence doomed to misfortune.

clue.text: Pet's fine after returning in good condition

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: fit means healthy, in good shape
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A pet animal recovering well after coming home in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet looks like an animal, but here it is a noun for a sulk or petty quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet (in a pet) is a fit of bad temper, and a tiff is a minor quarrel or huff.

clue.text: Simon oddly ignored by fellow American when winning

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters ignored, only the even ones remain

blocks.note: Victor is a man's name, a fellow
the second and fourth letters of Simon
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Simon gets the cold shoulder from his American countryman after winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow American' reads as one phrase, but splits into a man's name and the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorious means having won, triumphant.

clue.text: Completely destroy new ATM in Exeter

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed into a different order

blocks.note: all eleven letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A call to smash the new cash machine installed in the Devon city of Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placement word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To exterminate is to wipe out entirely, as with pests.

clue.text: Willing servant reportedly available immediately

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard by word of mouth, so the sound counts

blocks.note: ready means willing
a maid is a servant

explanation.surface: A keen servant who is said to be on hand at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made goods are prepared in advance, so can be had straight away.

clue.text: Wine containers found near the centre of Cirencester

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the middle letter

blocks.note: the sixth of eleven letters
hampers are wicker baskets

explanation.surface: Wine baskets turned up near the middle of Cirencester, a Cotswold town.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is an informal word for champagne, a sparkling wine.

clue.text: Nonsense contained in fancy polo club's code of etiquette

indicators.note: contained in means held inside something else
fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: rot is nonsense
the letters of polo, part of the fodder
C is the abbreviation for club

explanation.surface: Snobbish rubbish written into an upmarket polo club's rules of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal set of rules governing behaviour on official occasions.

clue.text: Difficult today to accept note on Swift being inflexible

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: hard means difficult
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
N is the abbreviation for note
swift and fast are synonyms

explanation.surface: It is hard nowadays to take a note about Jonathan Swift without being rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift, capitalised, looks like the satirist; it is just an adjective meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-and-fast rules are fixed and admit no exceptions, hence rigid.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge Carnera's title – not surprising at first

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken away
at first means the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the Italian form of address, Mr
the first letter of surprising

explanation.surface: Snubbing the boxer Carnera's title claim, which was no shock to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Primo Carnera was an Italian heavyweight boxing champion, so his title as a man is Signore.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is deliberately to take no notice of them.

clue.text: Spread untidily by Poles in short trousers – just the opposite

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter goes
in places one thing inside another, though here the next words flip which goes where
just the opposite swaps inside and outside, so the clothing goes within the compass points

blocks.note: S and N, the south and north poles
trews are tartan trousers

explanation.surface: Scattered about by Polish people wearing shorts, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' reverses the instruction: the trousers go inside the poles, not the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered carelessly over a surface.

clue.text: Dull sounding English officer

indicators.note: sounding means the word for dull is taken by how it is spoken

blocks.note: matt means dull, non-glossy, and is said the same as the other spelling
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tedious-sounding English army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: MATT (dull, as a paint finish) is said like its alternative spelling MAT, which then takes E.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a deck officer on a merchant ship, ranking below the captain.

clue.text: Perform just for the ears of Shakespeare perhaps

indicators.note: for the ears means the word is meant to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: to play is to perform
just means right, said the same as wright, a maker

explanation.surface: An instruction to act purely for an audience's ears, as on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A wright is a craftsman, as in wheelwright or shipwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is the most famous example of a dramatist, a writer of plays.

clue.text: Let out line and relax

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to ease off is to relax

explanation.surface: An angler pays out some line and takes it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease property is to let it out to a tenant for rent.

clue.text: Row with Bond on river

blocks.note: a tie is a bond
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: James Bond rowing out on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond, capitalised, suggests 007; it is a plain noun for a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one row in a set rising one above another, as in theatre seating.

clue.text: A Chilean revolutionary eating a bit of dessert from a dish

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned upside down, so the letters are overturned and rearranged
a bit of means only a small piece, here the opening letter
eating means swallowing something, so one piece ends up inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the first letter of dessert

explanation.surface: A Chilean rebel snacks on some pudding straight off the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes the Chilean as a rebel, but it scrambles the words A Chilean.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla with filling and sauce.

clue.text: Australia working to get energy from something found in the atmosphere

blocks.note: Oz is informal for Australia
a machine that is on is working
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Australia is working to harness energy from the air, perhaps via wind farms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen that forms a protective layer in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: SNP extremists against Labour's initial impulse to spend freely

indicators.note: extremists suggests the extreme ends, the first and last letters
initial means the very first letter only

blocks.note: the two ends of SNP
the first letter of Labour
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: Radical Scottish nationalists oppose Labour's opening bid to splash out on public spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party; 'extremists' fits the political surface but means its end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money lavishly on a spree.

clue.text: A rock band manager makes money keeping emphasis primarily on records

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece sits inside
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter alone

blocks.note: EPs are extended-play records
tin is slang for money
the first letter of emphasis

explanation.surface: A band manager earns cash by pushing records hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Epstein managed the Beatles; 'on records' places the money after the records in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein is the classic example of a pop group's manager, the man behind the Beatles.
